clue.text: One's principal teacher is God

indicators.note: the principal part of something is its chief or leading part, here the first letter of the word before

parts.note: its principal letter is O
sir is how a pupil addresses a male teacher, and so stands for one

explanation.surface: Someone declares that their headmaster is a deity, perhaps with tongue in cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's principal' is the first letter of 'One', O; 'teacher' is SIR, and 'is' stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian deity of the underworld and resurrection.

clue.text: Person occupying the boards even before The Good Old Days!

definitions.text: even before The Good Old Days!

indicators.note: the person takes up a place on the boards, so sits within them

parts.note: treading the boards means acting, so the boards are the stage
one means a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: An actor appears on stage in a nostalgic variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Good Old Days was a long-running BBC music-hall revival show; the definition jokes that something prehistoric predates even that.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric period, so far older than any old days anyone could remember fondly.

clue.text: Means to secure shore bird under rocks

indicators.note: in a down answer the bird is written below the rocks

parts.note: a reef is a ridge of rocks
the knot is a sandpiper found on shores

explanation.surface: A wading bird sits below a rocky outcrop on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot is a square knot used to tie two ends together securely.

clue.text: Heavy paste?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lumbering, walking in a clumsy heavy way
second meaning: paste is imitation jewellery, fake bling

explanation.walkthrough: Paste is glass used to imitate gems; the question mark warns that the second reading splits the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambling gait is awkward and heavy-footed, while paste jewels are fake glitter.

clue.text: Coal supply empty, requesting e.g. liquefied butane

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, so the letters of the word before are bent into a new order

parts.note: fodder taken as written

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides and leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: emptied, this leaves RG
e.g. means for example, which is 'as'

explanation.surface: The coal has run out, so someone asks for bottled gas such as butane instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not the noun but supple-ly, bending COAL into CALO; 'empty' strips 'requesting' to RG; 'e.g.' is AS. Calor Gas is a British brand of bottled gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Calor Gas is the trade name for bottled butane and propane sold in Britain for heaters and stoves.

clue.text: Participant in F1 GP campaign to cut ____?

definitions.text: Participant in F1 GP campaign to cut ____?

parts.note: a car competes in Formula One

indicators.note: the campaign cuts into the doctor, splitting it

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a doctor, slangily bones or sawbones
a mission is a campaign

explanation.surface: Racing cars at a Grand Prix taking part in a green campaign to reduce something left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: GP looks like Grand Prix after F1, but it is a doctor here. The blank is the answer itself: the campaign is one to cut carbon emissions.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing cars pump out exhaust gases, the pollution green campaigns aim to reduce.

clue.text: Porridge in the main ordered from AA motel

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order, rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone orders porridge from a motel approved by the Automobile Association.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, mostly used for porridge, which Americans call oatmeal.

clue.text: Warning from on high to beware Spooner's gross sentimentality

definitions.text: Warning from on high to beware

indicators.note: Spooner, famous for swapping the starts of words, signals the initial sounds trade places

parts.note: lardy means fat, gross
goo is sickly sentimentality

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for some very sloppy, oversentimental material.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer was the cry of old Edinburgh residents before tipping slops from upstairs windows, so the 'high' is an upper storey.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardyloo, from French 'gare de l'eau', warned passers-by that waste water was being thrown down from above.

clue.text: Duck shooter ignoring siren that is winding up exercise

indicators.note: the siren is ignored, so left out of the shooter

parts.note: taken as written
a hooter is a siren
id est is Latin for that is

indicators.note: in a down answer, winding up turns the piece upwards so it reads backwards

parts.note: PE is physical exercise

explanation.surface: A wildfowler ignores a warning and finishes a drill.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOOTER minus HOOTER leaves S. 'Duck' looks like the bird, but it is the verb, to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck an issue is to evade or dodge it, as a sidestep avoids a tackle.

clue.text: Elect blonde for Equity

parts.note: as in 'president elect', elect means chosen but yet to take office, that is 'to be'
fair-haired, so fair

explanation.surface: An actors' union asked to choose a blonde candidate for its post.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity is the British actors' union, which the capital letter exploits; here it is just the abstract quality of fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when conceding a point in the interests of fairness, i.e. for the sake of equity.

clue.text: In shop, vehicle allowed to go from scarlet to maroon?

indicators.note: the two pieces named before it go out of the word after, leaving only what remains

parts.note: the word from which the letters leave
a car is a vehicle
let means allowed
maroon is a shade of red

explanation.surface: In a shop, a car's paint is permitted to change from bright scarlet to a deeper maroon.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking CAR and LET from SCARLET leaves S; TO is as written; maroon is an example of RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods put in a store are kept in stock, which is what 'in shop' describes.

clue.text: Go and reserve a cycling activity for one's baby

parts.note: informally, to go is to urinate, to pee

indicators.note: letters cycle round from the front of the piece to its back, like a wheel turning

parts.note: to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and book a cycling session, apparently for one's infant.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOK + A cycled moves BOO to the end, giving KABOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo is the game of hiding the face and reappearing that adults play to amuse an infant.

clue.text: Stains plant OK

parts.note: to bed (out) is to plant in a bed
OK means yes

explanation.surface: Something says that stains on a plant are acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: BEDYE is an old word for dye thoroughly, and it is a verb here: 'Stains' is a third-person verb, not a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedye is an archaic word for to colour or tint something all over.

clue.text: Focus of amour in animation with final twist capturing heart of sailor-man

definitions.text: Focus of amour in animation with final twist capturing heart of sailor-man

indicators.note: the focus of something is its centre, here the middle letter of the word after

parts.note: its central letter is O

indicators.note: the twisted word takes the sailor's heart prisoner, holding it inside
the end of the word is twisted, so its last two letters change places

parts.note: lively means full of animation

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, the middle letter of the hyphenated word after

parts.note: nine letters, so its fifth letter, O, is the heart

explanation.surface: Describes the cartoon sweetheart of Popeye the Sailor Man, with a twist in the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Twisting the last two letters of LIVELY gives LIVEYL, which captures the O at the heart of 'sailor-man'; the O at the centre of 'amour' goes in front. Read whole, the clue describes Popeye's girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive Oyl is the cartoon girlfriend whom Popeye the Sailor Man adores in the animated films.

clue.text: Anticipated meet with toy company going bust

indicators.note: breaking apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meeting is expected with a toy firm that is going bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still to come lies in the future, so it is expected or awaited.

clue.text: First and second covered in wager

indicators.note: the second piece is covered over by the wager, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: Placing a bet on who comes first and second, as at a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The best is the top or leading one, in first place.

clue.text: Pour flighty type cracking ale

indicators.note: the insect breaks into the drink, so goes inside it

parts.note: ale is a beer
a moth is a flying creature

explanation.surface: Describes a moth getting into a glass of ale as it is poured.
explanation.walkthrough: To be mother is the British phrase for serving the tea, pouring it out for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever offers to 'be mother' takes the teapot and serves the drink for the group.

clue.text: Is after small and picturesque US city

indicators.note: the Is come after the small and

parts.note: two words for I: I itself and ego, the self

explanation.surface: Claims that something is pursuing a small, pretty American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is read as plural: two ways of saying I, I and EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a Californian coastal city noted for its beaches and attractive harbour.

clue.text: Order lacking in ball attached to hat ceremony

indicators.note: the decoration is missing from the bobble, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a pompom is the woolly ball on top of a hat
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Suggests a formal occasion where a hat with a bobble is worn without the proper honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is splendid ceremonial display, as in pomp and circumstance.

clue.text: Very good outside play area

indicators.note: the goodness goes round the outside of the play area

parts.note: pious means devout, morally good
rec is short for recreation ground, a playground

explanation.surface: Describes behaviour outside a playground as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' looks like one phrase, but 'Very' alone is the definition: precious little means very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious is used informally as an intensifying adverb, as in 'precious few', meaning extremely.

clue.text: Who's managing the local tunnelling of land army?

parts.note: a mine is a tunnel dug into the land
a host is an army, as in heavenly host

explanation.surface: Asks who manages the neighbourhood pub, while soldiers dig tunnels nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's nearby pub; mine host is the jocular title for its landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord who runs a public house is traditionally called mine host.

clue.text: Sparkling silver sedan

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a sedan chair is a litter, a covered chair carried on poles

explanation.surface: Describes a shiny silver car, a sedan being an American saloon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sedan' looks like a car but is the old sedan chair, carried by bearers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter means glittering, shining with sparkles of light.

clue.text: Curses stealing article in the course of visiting firm

indicators.note: happening during the visit, so placed inside it

parts.note: at as in at someone's house

indicators.note: the oath takes the article into itself

parts.note: damn is an oath, like 'curses!'
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone swears while burgling a company they are visiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is the adjective, unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means utterly resolute, refusing to be moved.

clue.text: Lines of verse in recital are distorted, I'm afraid

indicators.note: something in recital is spoken out, so we take how the word for the lines sounds

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem; spoken, it is heard as O-D

indicators.note: twisted out of shape, so the word before is rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A reciter is sorry that the lines of poetry are mangled in performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, ODE gives O + D, spelt OH D; ARE rearranged gives EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Oh dear' is an exclamation of regret, like apologising with 'I'm afraid so'.

clue.text: Caught by bed wearing woman's shorts

indicators.note: the woman's clothing wraps round what she is wearing, so these go inside

parts.note: she's means the woman is

indicators.note: the catch letter stands beside the bed, after it

parts.note: a cot is a bed
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricket image: caught near a bed, while a woman is wearing shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shorts' is a verb here: to scotch a plan is to cut it short or put an end to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch something is to thwart or curtail it, much as a short circuit stops a current.

clue.text: Right away we hear hinny's beginning to articulate this?

definitions.text: Right away we hear hinny's beginning to articulate this?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is H

indicators.note: to articulate is to joint or reshape, so the letters are moved into a new arrangement
the right is sent away, removed from the words after

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: We hear the start of a hinny's attempt to speak, and a donkey's bray comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: WE HEAR without R leaves WEHEA; with H from 'hinny', those six letters are rearranged. A hinny is the offspring of a stallion and a female donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Hee-haw is the braying call of a donkey, which a hinny, being half donkey, would make.

clue.text: Not even Bond drinks my great sherries!

indicators.note: the agent's remaining letters swallow the exclamation, so it goes inside them
says the following word is not there, so it is removed

parts.note: James Bond is agent 007, read as OO SEVEN
taken as written, the letters removed
lor is a dated exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
OS is outsize, the clothing abbreviation for very large

explanation.surface: Not even 007 could put away these splendid sherries, someone boasts.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond is read by his code number 007, spelt out as OO plus SEVEN, and 'Not even' is a deletion, not a comparison; 'my' is the old exclamation, as in 'Lor!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, rich style of Spanish sherry, aged with exposure to air.

clue.text: Location for showcasing what's essential to shout about?

definitions.text: Location for showcasing what's essential to shout about?

indicators.note: turned about, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: a spot is a location

indicators.note: the word for displays something inside it, as a case holds an exhibit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre, the middle letter

parts.note: five letters, so its middle letter is O

explanation.surface: Asks where to show off something that really must be announced loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: FOR holds O to give FOOR; SPOT FOOR read backwards gives the answer. The idiom is to shout something from the rooftops.
explanation.definitionFit: People proclaim news publicly from high places, hence the saying about shouting it from the tops of houses.

clue.text: Counterfeit banked by financiers at Zurich

indicators.note: the answer is held on either side by the words, as a river by its banks

explanation.surface: Fake money is deposited by Swiss bankers in Zurich.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior substitute or imitation, so it means fake.
